correctness.rationale: The complete finite-type recursion is exact because at each stage both directions of the one-move extension game must be met. In a separate direct two-sided EF replay, I matched fresh moves by adjacency to each previously chosen vertex and, where marked, by side; repeats can be answered by the existing image and place no additional constraint. The replay confirmed all 21 distinctions among parameters 1–7, the unmarked 7–8 identity, and the marked 8–9 identity (and marked 7–8 distinction). For the unbounded tail, the marked sum puts precisely the edges from earlier A to later B across factors. Local strategies run in parallel for at most four moves, and their union preserves all cross adjacencies and equality even when moves alternate between factors. Consequently the marked 8–9 identity propagates to every consecutive pair from 8 onward. Forgetting the marking and using the unmarked 7–8 identity gives exactly the claimed seven classes. Within the given family the smallest member of the saturated class is H_7 on 14 vertices.
residual_risks: The finite replay supplies the base decisions, while the symbolic sum supplies the tail. The 14-vertex minimum is only within the family, not among all graphs.
